corrected_fields.summary: This page describes the New York Fed's Open Market Trading Desk authority to conduct repo and reverse repo transactions as directed by the FOMC to implement monetary policy and maintain the fed funds rate within the target range. Repos temporarily increase reserve balances (economically similar to collateralized loans) while reverse repos temporarily reduce them (economically similar to collateralized borrowings). The Desk conducts overnight reverse repo (ON RRP) and standing repo (SRP) operations each business day at FOMC-set rates, serving as floor and ceiling mechanisms for money market rates respectively.
corrected_fields.why_it_matters: This page explains the foundational market plumbing mechanisms the Federal Reserve uses to control short-term interest rates. ON RRP and SRP operations create the corridor system (floor and ceiling) within which the fed funds rate operates. Understanding these mechanisms is essential for comprehending how monetary policy is transmitted to money markets and ultimately to broader financial conditions.
corrected_fields.market_structure_context: ON RRP and SRP form the technical framework for Fed policy implementation. ON RRP provides a floor by absorbing excess reserves when rates fall below IORB. SRP provides a ceiling by lending reserves when markets face upward rate pressure. Both operations use pre-announced rates set by the FOMC and are conducted daily by the Trading Desk. The page references transaction data published quarterly approximately two years after conduct per Dodd-Frank Act requirements.
